uncited: The Fourier Transform method converts a 3D scalar volume into the frequency domain to enable rendering via the Projection-Slice Theorem [Domain-transform methods](28-domain-transform-methods.md).
*   **Frequency Data:** A 3D array of complex numbers representing the frequency domain.
**Global Transformation (3D DFT):** Compute the 3D Discrete Fourier Transform of the volume.

**Slice Extraction:** According to the Projection-Slice Theorem, the 2D Fourier transform of a projection of the volume along a viewing direction is equal to a 2D slice through the origin of the 3D Fourier transform, perpendicular to the viewing direction [Domain-transform methods](28-domain-transform-methods.md).
Extract a 2D plane from the 3D frequency volume $F(u, v, w)$ corresponding to the viewing direction.
The extracted slice lies on a grid that may not align with the discrete 3D lattice of $F$.
Interpolation (e.g., trilinear or sinc) is required to resample the frequency data onto the 2D output grid [Domain-transform methods](28-domain-transform-methods.md).

**Inverse Transformation (2D IDFT):** Compute the 2D Inverse Discrete Fourier Transform of the extracted slice to obtain the spatial domain projection image [Domain-transform methods](28-domain-transform-methods.md).
*   **Boundary Artifacts:** The DFT assumes periodic boundary conditions.
Discontinuities at the volume boundaries cause high-frequency artifacts.

Mitigation includes zero-padding the volume by a factor of $k_2$ (typically $4/3$) and applying vignetting correction (premultiplying by the reciprocal of the interpolation filter response) [Domain-transform methods](28-domain-transform-methods.md).
The resolution must meet the Nyquist criterion relative to the volume's bandwidth [Domain-transform methods](28-domain-transform-methods.md).
*   **Hermitian Symmetry:** For real-valued input, the DFT output is Hermitian symmetric.
*   **Time Complexity:** The 3D DFT using FFT algorithms has a complexity of $O(N^3 \log N)$ for a volume of size $N^3$.
The 2D IDFT for an image of size $M \times M$ has a complexity of $O(M^2 \log M)$ [Domain-transform methods](28-domain-transform-methods.md).
*   **Memory Complexity:** The 3D frequency volume requires $O(N^3)$ memory [Domain-transform methods](28-domain-transform-methods.md).
Boundary artifacts require careful handling [Domain-transform methods](28-domain-transform-methods.md).
